transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this pre-air lock meeting started. We've got the finale going live Saturday at 9 PM Eastern, and the current voting draft has SMS and online portal voting open to our broadcast audience. I'll be making the final binding call on the voting package today, so I need to hear from standards, platform production, rights, and data protection before we lock this in. Who wants to kick things off?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something from the network's current standards memo, which was issued after the draft voting rules were circulated. The memo confirms three requirements: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. The current draft voting rules don't yet reflect these standards, so we need to make sure the final package incorporates them before we lock in today.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the results of the platform certification test I completed this morning. The SMS integration failed certification — it is not approved for use. The web portal passed certification, but the approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This means SMS voting cannot be included in the final package as things currently stand.

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue on the voting interface. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today, and it confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The current draft interface still contains performance clips, so those clips must be removed before we lock in the final package.

transcript.text: I need to flag a data protection issue before we lock this in. My privacy review, completed with the voting vendor this week, established two requirements that the current draft does not reflect. First, participation must be limited to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada — the draft still describes worldwide participation. Second, voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days — the draft currently has no deletion step at all. Both of these need to be incorporated into the final package.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text:
Thank you all for those critical flags. Let me make sure I have everything straight before I make the binding decision. Here's what I'm hearing:

1. From Julian (standards): Voters must be 13+, one vote per verified account, voting closes at 9:50 PM Eastern — none of this is in the current draft yet.
2. From Nia (platform): SMS failed certification and cannot be used. Only the web portal passed, and it requires account verification before accepting a vote.
3. From Leon (rights): We have label approval for finalist names and headshots only — no performance audio or video. Current draft still has performance clips that must be removed.
4. From Sofia (data protection): Participation must be limited to US and Canada only (not worldwide as the draft says), and voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days — no deletion step currently exists.

So the final package would need to be: web portal only (no SMS), account verification required, 13+ minimum age, one vote per verified account, voting closes 9:50 PM Eastern, US/Canada only, finalist names and headshots only (no performance clips), and voter identifiers deleted within 30 days.

Does anyone have anything to add or any concerns before I lock this in? If not, I'll settle the final voting package now.
